text: The ancestors of Aboriginal Australians arrived in Australia more than 50,000 years ago.
Back then Australia was joined to New Guinea by land, but they still had to cross the sea.
src: Archaeology shows that their ancestors arrived 50,000 to 65,000 years ago
They came when Australia was part of Sahul, joined to New Guinea by land, but still had to cross the sea beyond the Wallace Line

text: Over time they became hundreds of peoples, each with its own language and its own land, called Country.
They pass down stories of creation, called the Dreaming, through dance, songs, stories and art.
src: Over time the people formed as many as 500 linguistic and territorial groups / Each language and its people are connected with a stretch of territory known as Country
Traditional beliefs are passed down and shared through dance, stories, songlines and art, which together tell of creation in the Dreaming, or Dreamtime

text: About 4,000 years ago their stone tools grew smaller, and new languages spread across the land.
Aboriginal peoples traded goods with each other across the whole continent.
src: About 4,000 years ago the dingo arrived, the Pama-Nyungan languages spread and stone tools grew smaller
Long before Britain came, Aboriginal peoples traded across the continent

text: More than 350 years ago, fishers from Indonesia sailed to the north coast and brought dugout canoes.
From 1788 settlers from Britain took the land, and disease and fighting killed many Aboriginal people, who fought back.
src: from the mid-1660s Indonesian fishing vessels visited the north coast for trepang, bringing dugout canoes and metal harpoon heads

British colonisation began at Port Jackson in 1788 with the First Fleet / Settlers claimed the land as their exclusive possession / 90% of Indigenous Australians died from introduced disease and violent conflict with the colonists / Aboriginal people fought back

text: Many Aboriginal children were taken from their families, and in 2008 Prime Minister Kevin Rudd said sorry for this.
Today Aboriginal people have won back many rights, and they own or share about half of Australia's land.
src: between 1910 and 1970 between 10 and 33 percent of Aboriginal children were removed from their families / Prime Minister Kevin Rudd made a formal apology for the Stolen Generations in 2008
since 1967 and the Mabo decision have won back rights and much of their land / By 2021 Indigenous Australians held exclusive or shared title to about 54% of the land
